tldr: Survey responses from Oregon business owners, government representatives, and non-profit leaders on state economic competitiveness. Dominant themes: high tax burden (especially Corporate Activity Tax), excessive regulations and permitting delays unfavorably comparing to Texas, Arizona, Colorado, and Florida. Respondents advocate tax relief, streamlined permitting, apprenticeship/vocational education expansion, land use law updates, and stronger state economic development strategy. Workforce shortages noted as critical. Overall sentiment: Oregon's regulatory and tax environment is driving business departures and deterring investment relative to competitor states.

bullets.text: Corporate Activity Tax criticized by multiple business respondents as excessive burden disproportionately affecting small and medium enterprises
Respondents cite permitting delays and complex regulatory compliance requirements as major barriers to business development and site readiness
Future Ready Oregon program noted as approximately $200 million investment focused on workforce development, training, and equitable career pathways
Multiple respondents recommend Enterprise Zone expansion with broader eligibility and tax incentives to compete with states like Texas and Arizona
Apprenticeship program expansion and vocational education cited as critical workforce needs to address shortages and talent retention in Oregon
Respondents compare Oregon unfavorably to Texas, Arizona, Colorado, and Florida on business-friendliness, regulatory burden, and cost of operations
Climate Protection Program described by one respondent as costing businesses and consumers between $500 million to $1 billion annually
